newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS PARTY DISSOLVES SEVEN STATE UNITS

Congress party president Sitaram Kesri dissolved the party's state committees (PCCs) in seven states. Observers were appointed to report on the party setup in these states before constituting the new committees. A decision was taken recently to replace PCC chiefs in states where the party failed to get more than 30 percent of votes polled in the 1996 national elections. Kesri, however, avoided any changes in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh where the party polled 11.26 and 5.8 percent votes, respectively. Dissolution of the Delhi PCC, despite the Congress getting 37.29 percent of the votes, followed the party's debacle in the recent municipal elections.
The Pioneer
PRESSURE ON PREMIER TO AXE UTTAR PRADESH GOVERNOR

Pressure was mounting on the prime minister to remove the Uttar Pradesh governor, Romesh Bhandari. The move gathered momentum after Bhandari took exception to criticism by the home minister, who said there was complete anarchy in the state. Notwithstanding the fact that Bhandari was appointed by the defence minister, the governor's style of functioning came in for severe criticism at the ruling coalition's Parliamentary Party meeting. Sources, however, said the defence minister was unmoved by the home minister's indictment.
The Economic Times
INDIA MAY SLIP ON PETROLEUM IMPORTS

Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) informed the government it would be unable to pay for oil imports after April if nothing was done to improve its financial position. IOC, India's canalising agent for all petroleum imports, presently had a foreign exchange exposure ceiling of $2.9 billion. The finance ministry had recently raised IOC's exposure limit from $2.5 billion against the oil major's demand for a hike to $3.5 billion. Latest reports indicated IOC would be allowed to raise an additional $0.6 billion as foreign currency loans from Indian banks. The oil-import bill was expected to touch $9 billion this year against an estimated $7.5 billion earlier.
SLACK REFORMS FAIL TO BUDGET EXPECTATIONS

Corporates seemed upbeat on the eve of the 1997/98 budget with senior executives expecting the finance minister to present a plan favourable to business and industry. An overwhelming majority felt the pace of economic reforms to be too slow. A pre-budget survey of senior executives in private and government firms found 55 percent expecting the budget to be favourable to business and industry. However, 31 percent expected the budget to be unfavourable to business and industry. Forty percent of the respondents wanted aboilition of the minimum alternate tax. A similar proportion felt abolishing dividend tax could galvanise the markets.
BUDGET NOT TO IMPACT MARKET: MORGAN STANLEY

The stock market was expected fare well even if the budget failed to deliver some of the key expectations. A Morgan Stanley report said there was very little buying on expectation of positive developments in the budget. This minimised the risk of a major selloff due to disappointment with the actual proposals. It felt investors stayed away from major commitments this time around due to losses sustained in post-budget sessions in each of the previous four years.
EXTERNAL DEBT DIPS TO 28.7 PCT

India's external debt indicators improved during 1995/96 (April-March) and the total debt stock declined too. The ratio of external debt to GDP, steadily declining from its peak of 41 percent in 1991/92, fell below the critical 30 percent figure for moderately indebted countries to 28.7 percent in 1995/96. The total stock of debt was also down from the peak of $99.01 billion at the end of March 1995 to $92.2 billion at March 1996 end.
Financial Express
GENERAL INSURANCE CORP MAY LOWER TARIFF RATES

General Insurance Corporation (GIC) has hiked the third-party motor premium by 215-799 percent for various categories of vehicles. However, it planned to revise its tariff structure downward for the rest of the tariff-based products. Despite the hike, GIC and its four subsidiaries were bearing a 80 percent loss in its third-party motor portfolio, sources said. The industry's projected loss during fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) was pegged around 400 percent, as compared to 395 percent in the previous year.
VIDEOCON FILES WIND UP CASE AGAINST SHAW WALLACE

The Videocon group filed winding up petitions against Shaw Wallace & Co (SWC) before the Calcutta High Court for the recovery of around 50 million rupees. The petitions, soliciting appointment of a provisional liquidator, were filed by two Videocon group firms, Tapti Machines and Videocon Leasing and Finance. The petitions would be heard by the court within two months. Criminal proceedings against SWC filed by the two Videocon companies were already pending before the a Bombay court.
OIL INDIA TO OPT OUT OF BRAHMAPUTRA EXPLORATION

The award of the north bank of the Brahmaputra oilfield, the only field left in the joint venture exploration round, has taken a new twist. The state-owned Oil India Limited (OIL) has asked the Petroleum Ministry to withdraw the field from the joint venture round, more than 14 months after it was put on the bidding block. OIL cited antagonising the local industry as a reason for seeking the withdrawal, it was learnt. Ministry sources, however, dismissed the reason as being unjustified, considering the fact that the Kumchai block, also in Assam, was being successfully operated by the private sector for over three years now.
Business Standard
SUBSCRIPTION FLOOR FOR ISSUES MAY BE WAIVED

Bourse regulator SEBI was considering allowing companies to decide the level of an issue's success. SEBI was expected to discuss the move with the department of company affairs. Though the Companies Act allowed firms to decide the level of success, one of the rules stipulated that unless an issue garnered 90 percent of the issue amount, funds would have to be refunded to the investor. Similar provisions existed in the SEBI guidelines too. Allowing either of the two options would also ensure issuers did not resort to moves like backdating applications to see the issues through.
STATE-OWNED LIFE INSURANCE ENTITY PROPOSED

The parliamentary standing committee on finance may recommend creation of another life insurance company in the public sector. The committee, deliberating on the bill to give statutory powers to the Insurance Regulatory Authority of India (IRAI), is expected to submit its report on March 7, 1997. The committee is, however, divided over the bill on IRAI. Some members are in favour of blocking the bill altogether until the government clearly assures that foreign insurance companies will not be allowed entry into the industry. A few members are, however, of the view that the bill will do no harm.
MARKET EXPECTATIONS HIGH ON BUDGET-EVE

Budget pressures were visible on the Bombay bourse sensitive index again, with the pre-budget expectations in the run-up becoming stronger. Though the pre-budget week witnessed some fresh buying activity, market sentiments was weak enough for any positive announcement to push the index and the capital markets in an uptrend. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) remained away from the markets in the pre-budget trading. But, a section of the FIIs felt the removal of the double taxation on dividends, buy-back of shares and a partial opening up of the insurance sector could aid the revival of the capital markets.
The Observer
STEEL AUTHORITY PLANS $350 MLN BORROWING

Steel Authority of India (SAIL) planned a $350 million External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) to meet its proposed expansions in the Ninth Plan period. Once SAIL got the necessary approval from the Finance Ministry, the company would take a decision on the lead managers for the issue. The ECB move formed part of SAIL's plan of infusing 150 billion rupees into the company in the Ninth Plan period for its expansions in various units. This would increase the company's steel-making capacity from 10 million tonnes to 17 million tonnes over the next 10 years.
TAXING TIME AHEAD FOR THE RICH

The government may widen the scope of a federal expenditure tax to cover luxury items and high-end consumer durables. Analysts felt luxury or expenditure tax would be politically accepted and would not hurt market sentiment too much. New targets could include cigarettes, high-end consumer durables, air travel, liquor and five-star hotels. Automobiles, particularly diesel luxury cars, could take the biggest hit. They felt higher levies, whether in the form of increased duties or an expenditure tax, would hurt the demand for diesel cars.
EQUITIES FLARE ON HOPE BEFORE BUDGET

Equities flared up on the Bombay bourse (BSE), following fresh speculative support and short covering by bear operators on the budget-eve. Reflecting the bullish mood, the 30-share BSE index opened at 3,379.10 and flared up to close at 3,427.87 points, registering a 63 point gain. With both the Economic Survey and the centrl bank's report on currency and finance talking about the sluggish capital market, market players were hopeful of the finance minister announcing some measures to boost the market.
Business Line
BUDGET LIKELY TO PRUNE SMALL INDUSTRY LIST

The government was set to prune the list of 836 items reserved for the small scale sector. Sources said the announcement to throw open about 280 items -- currently reserved for the small sector -- to manufacture by large units in collaboration with foreign partners was likely to be part of the budget. A notification on the items being taken out of the small sector fold would be simultaneously issued. A majority of the items earmarked for dereservation were expected to pertain to the agro and food processing sectors.
